edges.reason: Owned constructor assigns owner from the untrusted msg.sender value.
onlyOwner modifier compares msg.sender to owner before transferOwnership executes.
acceptOwnership requires msg.sender == newOwner, gating the ownership takeover.
onlyOwner modifier checks msg.sender before transferAnyERC20Token executes.
transfer debits balances[msg.sender] using the caller-supplied address.
approve writes allowed[msg.sender][spender] keyed by the caller address.
approveAndCall keys the allowance by msg.sender before the external call.
transferFrom deducts allowed[from][msg.sender] using the caller as spender.
msg.sender is forwarded as the from argument into the external receiveApproval call.
Owned constructor writes owner = msg.sender.
transferOwnership writes the pending owner into newOwner.
acceptOwnership reads newOwner for the authorization check and clears it.
acceptOwnership overwrites owner with newOwner.
Stored newOwner flows into the msg.sender == newOwner requirement of acceptOwnership.

Token constructor sets the name state variable.
Token constructor sets the decimals state variable.
Token constructor sets _totalSupply to the fixed mint amount.
Token constructor mints the whole supply into balances of the initial holder.
transfer updates the balances mapping for sender and recipient.
approve writes the allowance into the allowed mapping.
transferFrom updates balances of from and to.
transferFrom decreases the spender allowance in the allowed mapping.
approveAndCall writes the allowance into the allowed mapping.
totalSupply reads balances[address(0)] when computing the circulating supply.
totalSupply reads the _totalSupply state variable.
balanceOf returns the value read from the balances mapping.
allowance returns the nested value read from the allowed mapping.
transfer reads the current balances before debiting and crediting.
transferFrom reads balances of from and to.
transferFrom reads the current allowance of the spender.
transferAnyERC20Token reads owner as the destination of the rescued tokens.

transfer credits the recipient parameter.
transfer uses the tokens amount parameter.
approve uses the spender parameter as allowance key.
approve stores the tokens amount as allowance.
transferFrom debits the from parameter balance.
transferFrom credits the to parameter balance.
transferFrom uses the tokens amount parameter.
allowance uses tokenOwner as the outer mapping key.
allowance uses spender as the inner mapping key.
approveAndCall passes the caller-supplied spender address to the external call target.
approveAndCall stores and forwards the tokens parameter.
approveAndCall forwards the arbitrary data parameter to the callee.
transferAnyERC20Token uses the caller-supplied tokenAddress as the external call target.
transferAnyERC20Token forwards the tokens parameter to the external transfer.
safeAdd writes the sum into its local result variable c.
safeSub writes the difference into its local result variable c.
safeMul writes the product into its local result variable c.
safeDiv writes the quotient into its local result variable c.
balanceOf returns through the named local variable balance.
allowance returns through the named local variable remaining.
transfer invokes safeSub for balance debits.
transfer invokes safeAdd for balance credits.
transferFrom invokes safeSub for balances and allowance deduction.
transferFrom invokes safeAdd to credit the recipient.
The raw _totalSupply value flows into the unchecked subtraction.
balances[address(0)] flows into the unchecked subtraction without SafeMath.
The unchecked subtraction result is returned by totalSupply.
approveAndCall transfers control to an arbitrary external contract before returning.
The spender parameter determines the callee address of the external receiveApproval call.
The callee invoked by receiveApproval can re-enter approveAndCall or other SparksterToken functions.
transferAnyERC20Token transfers control to an arbitrary external token contract.
The tokenAddress parameter determines the callee address of the external transfer call.
The called token contract can call back into the token contract during the external transfer.
